subject: Qualification + model selection: request for customer prompts and edge-case examples
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Samir Khanna <samir@innovamed.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Jul 2028 15:12:00 +0000
Subject: Qualification + model selection: request for customer prompts and edge-case examples

Hi Samir — great conversation today, thanks for the time. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on scope for the evaluation: 

Summary of needs:
- Primary use case: summarization + patient-facing guideline generation from internal clinical notes and product spec sheets.
- Volume: ~10k queries/day currently, bursty around end of month reporting.
- SLO: 95th latency target ~600ms for short responses (<=150 tokens).
- Quality constraints: avoid hallucinations on dosage/contraindications; strict PII handling.

Recommended evaluation plan (what we need from you):
1) Share a representative prompt set (100–300 rows) covering: common queries, rare/edge queries, expected redactions, and examples that previously failed. CSV template attached.
2) Mark any prompts that contain PHI/PII or regulated content (or send sanitized+original if policy allows).
3) If possible, include 10–20 labeled failure cases where the current model produced incorrect or unsafe outputs.

Redwood deliverables (what we will provide):
- Shortlist of 2–3 model variants we expect to test (open-weights + quantized variants) with rough perf/cost tradeoffs.
- Benchmark run against a privacy-preserving subset + model-fit notes and recommended guardrails.
- Example prompt engineering patterns and redaction guidance for your ingestion pipeline.

Attachments: innovamed_prompt_template.csv (simple CSV with columns: id, raw_prompt, sanitized_prompt, expected_output, failure_flag, notes) and a short runtime/benchmark summary we will populate after the first run.

Next steps / asks for Samir: please upload the filled template and any labeled failure examples to the Drive link below by EOD Thu (2028-07-12) if possible. If you have legal/privacy questions, loop privacy@innovamed.com and we can include our security SMEs.

Links: HubSpot deal and shared Drive folder included below.

Thanks — I’ll draft a precise eval plan and model list once we have the sample prompts.

Best,
Ben
Ben Carter | Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: innovamed_prompt_template.csv]
[Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2bBenchmarkDocs]

From: Samir Khanna <samir@innovamed.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Jul 2028 17:45:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Qualification + model selection: request for customer prompts and edge-case examples

Ben — thanks for the clear note. We'll prioritize this. A few clarifications from our side: 

- We can provide a 200-row CSV exported from our ticketing/search logs; about ~30 rows will need redaction before sending.
- For failure cases, we have an internal tracker (internal IDs) — I will export 12 representative failures and flag them.
- Legal asked for a short one-pager from Redwood describing how you handle inference cache, retention, and whether raw prompts are stored for longer than 30 days. Can you attach that?

I'll aim to get the files uploaded to the Drive folder by Wednesday EOD (2028-07-12 PT) and will loop privacy@innovamed.com if we need guidance on redaction.

Samir
Samir Khanna | Head of AI Platforms | Innovamed
[Attachment: none yet]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Samir Khanna <samir@innovamed.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Jul 2028 09:30:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Qualification + model selection: request for customer prompts and edge-case examples

Samir — perfect, appreciate the quick turnaround. Quick answers to legal + what we’ll include in the eval pack: 

Legal / retention note (short):
- Redwood's hosted evaluation runs use short-lived KV caches; by default, raw prompts in the hosted flow are retained for 30 days for debugging and quality analysis and then purged.
- We can offer a private evaluation (VPC) where you control storage and retention if that is required by Innovamed policy.

Initial model shortlist we recommend testing (will finalize after seeing prompts):
- OpenPhi-XL (base open checkpoint) — best baseline for instruction-following on clinical text.
- OpenPhi-XL quantized (4-bit) — runs ~2.3x cheaper with modest quality delta; good for throughput testing.
- LlamaMed-7B-8k — smaller, lower-latency option for short responses.

Benchmark plan and deliverables:
- We’ll run a 3-model microbenchmark on the sanitized subset + the 12 failure cases you export. Results: latency P50/P95, token-cost estimate, and a small quality matrix (precision on factual fields, hallucination rate on the sample).
- Deliverable: single PDF with results, per-model tradeoffs, and recommended production guardrails + a short prompt-redaction template (attached).

Prompt collection ask (practical):
- Use the attached template and include columns for: expected_output_type, must_preserve_fields, any redaction rules applied. If you can mark true PHI rows in a separate column that helps our internal eval labeling.

If Innovamed prefers not to upload original PHI to hosted Drive, we can accept a locally redacted CSV + a hashed id map and run the private eval. Let me know which you prefer.

I’ve attached the initial runtimes summary — it's a placeholder and we'll populate with your data. Also linking our short model-fit explainer for clinical workloads.

Next step: Samir uploads CSV; we run a 48–72 hour microbenchmark and deliver results + recommendations.

Thanks — looping Marissa and Stephanie to help schedule the benchmark and security check.

Ben
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachments: innovamed_prompt_template.csv, runtimes_benchmark_summary.pdf]
[Related link: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/DEAL-4297]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Jul 2028 20:12:00 +0000
Subject: Internal: Innovamed eval — PII redaction + labeling notes

Marissa / Steph — internal note before we ingest anything from Innovamed: 

- Expect ~25% of their rows to contain sensitive patient identifiers. When Samir uploads, please run a quick redaction check (script in our shared playbook) and flag any rows where the redaction changes the meaning of the prompt (we should surface these to the customer).
- For the 12 failure cases, prioritize labeling the output field that caused the failure (e.g., wrong dosage, invented contraindication). That will help our quality regression checks.
- Plan: run microbench on hosted infra with sanitized data first. If legal requests private eval, pivot to VPC and coordinate keys with Account Ops.

I’ve added the redaction template and a short checklist in the Drive folder. Once we have the uploaded CSV, Marissa can kick off the runner and I’ll prep the evaluation job.

Ben
[Attachment: innovamed_prompt_template.csv]
